To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in India, where the majority of the population is currently undernourished and the wealthiest consume a diet high in meat and dairy, shifting to a healthy diet would increase environmental footprints of food production, but that this increase would be much smaller than that seen if the whole population were to adopt a diet consumed by the wealthiest.

In India, where both under-nutrition, and obesity and overweight are simultaneously prevalent, shifting current national food patterns towards healthier diets (in line with dietary guidelines) would lead to small increases of about 3–6% in the greenhouse gas (GH) emissions, water footprints and land use (L) of the food system.

in India, where there is both undernutrition and overweight and obesity, shifting from current dietary patterns to healthy diets would increase environmental impacts of food production by 3-5%, but would decrease these impacts by 6-16% among those who currently eat above recommended levels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the environmental impacts of dietary shifts.
the potential environmental impacts of dietary shifts that would result in improved population health in India.
the environmental implications of the adoption of healthy diets in India.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the adoption of healthy diets in India is likely to lead to only a small increase in the environmental foot prints of the food system.
dietary changes that are beneficial for health in India may also lead to increases in environmental footprints of food production.

dietary shifts in India could lead to increased environmental footprints of food production, though the size and distribution of the effects would depend upon the dietary changes adopted and the baseline dietary patterns of the population.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the environmental impact of dietary changes is not linear.
the environmental impacts of a shift to healthy diets are small in comparison to the potential benefits to health.
dietary shifts in India could have substantial environmental impacts, and these impacts vary by dietary scenario and sub-region.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a need to consider the environmental impacts of dietary changes, especially when the diets are those of the wealthiest.
the environmental impacts of dietary shifts are highly dependent on the dietary pattern being adopted.
the food system is complex, and the impacts of dietary shifts are context specific and depend on the baseline dietary patterns of the population.
